newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to revise debt to energy firms as bonds.
newsitem.headline: Russia to revise debt to energy firms as bonds.

text.p: Russia will restructure state debts to energy firms, including gas group Gazprom, by issuing bonds to the companies concerned, First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko said on Friday.
"The point is to restructure debts of federal consumers to energy firms, oil companies and Gazprom," he told a news conference.
Asked when the Gazprom bonds would be issued he said: "I am almost certain in 1997."
He added the Gazprom bonds would begin maturing in 2003.

Kiriyenko did not say whether the bonds would -- or could -- be traded but added that the government, which has approved the programme in a new order, believed companies could use the bonds as collateral on loans from foreign financial institutions.

The government is trying to account for old state debts to the energy sector and begin paying on time for current energy use, Kiriyenko said, calling the move a civilised attempt to fix the amount of the debt despite the government's lack of cash.
The government order calls for separate spending provisions to cover government energy use in the 1998 budget and spending plans for the second half of the year, he said.
He said the state would have to negotiate debts claimed by the energy firms, which would include debts by federal users for which the federal government was not directly responsible.
"For example, there is a 70 trillion rouble debt by federal consumers owed to Gazprom -- but for what part of that should the state answer?" he asked.
